hero.title: Placeholders
hero.subtitle: Dynamic text you can drop into welcome messages, leave messages, tags, and ticket messages -- resolved live every time Commie sends them.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.p1: A placeholder is a small piece of text wrapped in curly braces, like {user.mention}, that Commie replaces with real information the moment a message is sent -- who joined, which server, how many members it has, and more.
gettingStarted.p2: You'll find them in four places: the welcome message (/welcome message), the leave message (/leave message), tag content (/tag create and /tag update), and a ticket's opening message (/ticket message). Any command tagged "Placeholders available" on the Commands page supports everything on this guide.
gettingStarted.p3: You don't need to write any code -- just type the placeholder where you want the value to appear, save the command, and Commie fills it in automatically.

syntax.title: Syntax
syntax.basicBody: The simplest placeholders take no arguments -- just a name in braces. They're replaced with a single value.
syntax.argsBody: Some placeholders take arguments, separated by semicolons: {name:arg1;arg2}. Use these to transform text or build embeds piece by piece.
syntax.nestedBody: Placeholders can contain other placeholders as arguments, resolved from the inside out.
syntax.escapeBody: To show a literal brace instead of triggering a placeholder, escape it with a backslash: \{ and \}.
syntax.fallbackBody: A misspelled or unrecognized placeholder is never an error -- it's left exactly as typed, so you can see and fix the typo.

reference.title: Placeholders
reference.subtitle: Every placeholder Commie currently understands, grouped by what it does.

ref.userId: The message author's Discord user ID.
ref.userMention: A clickable mention of the message author.
ref.userDiscriminator: The author's legacy discriminator ("0" for current-style usernames).
ref.userAvatar: The URL of the author's current display avatar.
ref.userTag: The author's full tag, e.g. username#0.
ref.guildName: The current server's name, or "DM" outside a server.
ref.guildId: The current server's ID, or "DM" outside a server.
ref.guildIcon: The current server's icon URL, empty if it has none.
ref.channelMention: A clickable mention of the current channel, empty in DMs.
ref.title: Converts Text To Title Case.
ref.length: Returns how many characters the text has.
ref.repeat: Repeats text a number of times (0-10).
ref.sum: Adds together any number of values.
ref.sub: Subtracts the second value from the first.
ref.div: Divides the first value by the second ("undefined" if dividing by zero).
ref.embedTitle: Starts a new embed with this title.
ref.embedDescription: Sets the description of the current embed.
ref.embedColor: Sets the current embed's color from a hex code, with or without "#".
ref.embedFooter: Sets the footer text of the current embed.
ref.embedImage: Sets the main image of the current embed.
ref.embedThumbnail: Sets the thumbnail of the current embed.
ref.embedField: Adds a field to the current embed. Set the third argument to "false" for a full-width field.
ref.emoji: Reacts to the sent message with this emoji once it's posted.
ref.if: Returns the second argument if the first is truthy, otherwise the third (or nothing).

limits.title: Limits
limits.item1: Placeholders can nest up to 15 levels deep -- beyond that, the innermost one is left as literal text instead of resolving, guarding against runaway templates.
limits.item2: {repeat:text;times} clamps "times" between 0 and 10, even if you ask for more.
limits.item3: Embed fields built with {embed.field:...} follow Discord's own limits: 256 characters for a title, 4096 for a description, 1024 for a field value, and a maximum of 25 fields per embed.
limits.item4: If a function placeholder throws an internal error, it silently resolves to an empty string instead of breaking the rest of your message.
limits.item5: Only the first 10 embeds and first 20 reactions produced by a single render are actually sent, matching Discord's own per-message limits.
